standard.title: Language reflects cultural practices
standard.description: notice that people use language in ways that reflect cultural practices
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have noticed connections between language and culture (AC9LSF03) and that greetings carry cultural meaning (AC9LS2C04). They have not yet explored the diversity of target language communities, regional language variation, or the relationship between language use and cultural identity more broadly.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students notice that people use language in ways that reflect cultural practices — across the diversity of target language communities, in formal and informal contexts, and in relation to First Nations Australian and other cultural practices.

nodes.label: Diversity of target language communities and variation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notice that the target language is spoken in many different communities and that language use varies across these communities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two target language communities or countries and at least one way language varies between them.
nodes.typical_width: Locate target language communities on a world map; recognise that the target language is spoken with cultural and linguistic variation across many communities; notice vocabulary or expression differences across regions; understand that some people speak more than one language.
wider: Research one specific target language community — find two or three cultural practices reflected in the language used there and share findings
Compare the symbols and expressions of two target language communities — identify what they reveal about each community's identity
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that the target language is spoken by diverse communities — not a single monolithic culture — is the conceptual foundation for all subsequent cultural and intercultural work. Students who imagine a single homogeneous target language culture cannot engage with genuine cultural complexity.

response_modes.reason: Diversity awareness is built by encountering multiple communities and language variation examples. Single-community exposure produces a narrow and misleading picture of the target language.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two target language communities and locates them on a world map
Identifies at least one way language varies across target language communities

nodes.label: Language, identity and First Nations connections
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notice how language use reflects cultural practices and identity — including formal and informal contexts, First Nations Australian language connections, and their own multilingual or multicultural backgrounds.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one way that language use in the target language reflects a cultural practice; connect First Nations Australian language to place and identity.
nodes.typical_width: Explore cultural practices reflected in target language use — celebrations, family practices, address conventions; engage with First Nations language connections to Country; compare students' own ways of expressing identity; discuss belonging to multiple communities.
wider: Find one local First Nations place name and research its meaning — connect this to the idea that language carries the history and identity of a community

Compare ways of expressing cultural identity across the student's own background, a target language community and a First Nations Australian community — find at least one meaningful similarity and one difference

response_modes.reason: Language-identity connections are most visible across multiple cultural contexts — the student's own, target language communities and First Nations communities. Each comparison point illuminates the pattern from a different angle.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Connecting students' own multilingual and multicultural identities to the language-culture connections in the target language positions language learning as personally relevant. The First Nations language connection is particularly important in the Australian context.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one way that language use in the target language reflects a cultural practice and explains the connection
Identifies that First Nations Australians have languages connected to Country and can give at least one local example
